text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000042's 99215 share is elevated across every complexity stratum and concentrated on 0-1 condition patients, which is consistent with upcoding, but documentation is too thin to confirm.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The billing pattern, not the charts, drives this leaning. The 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with no chronic conditions. Most 99215s fall on low-complexity patients, for example single-complaint visits coded R21, M54.50 or N39.0 (C0025265, C0025592, C0026866), where a high-complexity visit would be unusual. The provider does treat some genuinely complex patients (C0025391, C0025824), but their 99215 share is elevated even there, so panel acuity alone does not explain the excess. The documentation neither supports nor undercuts this: only 2 documented 99215 claims came back, both supported (C0025546, C0026261), and the data-reviewed check raised no flags. That is far too few charts to judge. A reviewer should first request records specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed here and compare the documented MDM and time against the billed level."}
